exposure: pre-existing chronic health conditions in parents
atypical development in the first six months of life (e.g., hypotonia)
cohort: The study utilized data from the Australian Autism Biobank, including autistic children aged 2-17, their siblings, parents, and unrelated controls.
finding: Advanced maternal age, male sex at birth, CALD background, parental pre-existing chronic health conditions, paternal medication use before conception, pregnancy complications, caesarean delivery, maternal medication use during pregnancy, and early-life health issues were associated with an increased risk of ASD.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was found to be associated with ASD risk.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for children aged 2-17 years.
